title: NASA Administrator to Fly Over NFL Game and Greet Fans at MetLife Stadium
summary: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will pilot an F-5 jet in a flyover before the Jets vs. Browns game in New Jersey, while NASA staff meet fans outside the stadium. The appearance is part of the agency's Inspiration Tour, which builds toward a big public air and space event in Florida.

sections.heading: Flyover to Open the Game
sections.body: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will pilot one of three F-5 fighter jets to kick off the New York Jets vs. Cleveland Browns game in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday, Oct. 11. The flyover is part of the agency's Inspiration Tour. Isaacman will also be available for limited media interviews during the game.

sections.heading: Meeting Fans Before Kickoff
sections.body: NASA team members will be at the agency's Experience Zone, located at the Jets Tailgate Zone outside the stadium, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. EDT before the game. Fans can learn about NASA's return to the Moon under the Artemis dome, play interactive games, and take photos with a large inflatable SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. SLS is the rocket tied to the agency's Artemis lunar plans.

sections.heading: What the Inspiration Tour Does
sections.body: The Inspiration Tour makes stops across the country and brings together academic, industry, and public sector stakeholders. Its goal is to connect NASA with the people, technologies, and organizations that drive American leadership in space.

sections.heading: MAX POWER Finale in Florida
sections.body: The tour will end with MAX POWER, a public exposition of American air and space innovation, on Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8. It will take place on and near Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Held in honor of America's 250th anniversary, the family-friendly event will showcase next-generation aircraft, spacecraft, autonomous vehicles, and technologies that will help shape the future of transportation in air and space.

source.name: NASA
source.original_title: NASA to Conduct Flyover, Engage NFL Fans at MetLife Stadium
